deep.reconstruction:
This folio is a draft of §§20-22 of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). It does two things. First, it proves that the real part of the quadratic form in the period matrix a_{mu,nu} is negative definite, which is needed for the convergence of the theta series. Second, it counts the zeros of theta on the cut surface T'. Riemann writes S' for T'.

(A) Positivity via the Dirichlet integral.
- Let w = mu + i*nu be an everywhere-finite integral (first-kind integral) on the cut surface S'.
- Its periodicity modulus across cut a_nu is A^(nu) = alpha_nu + i*gamma_nu. Across cut b_nu it is B^(nu) = beta_nu + i*delta_nu.
- By Cauchy-Riemann (nu_y = mu_x, nu_x = -mu_y; implicit step, mine): mu_x^2 + mu_y^2 = mu_x*nu_y - mu_y*nu_x.
- So the Dirichlet integral ∫∫(mu_x^2+mu_y^2) dS equals ∫∫ d(mu)∧d(nu) over S'.
- By Green/Stokes this equals ∮ mu d nu taken positively around the boundary of S'.
- The boundary consists of the two banks of each cut, so the integral is Σ ∫(mu^+ - mu^-) d nu along the cuts a, b (and c).
- Along a_nu the jump mu^+ - mu^- is the constant alpha_nu. Integrating dnu along a_nu gives the imaginary part of the b_nu-period, delta_nu.
- Along b_nu the jump is beta_nu and ∫dnu = -gamma_nu.
- Along the c-cuts the jumps are constant and ∫dnu = 0 (implicit).
- Result: ∫∫(mu_x^2+mu_y^2) dS = Σ_{nu=1}^p (alpha_nu*delta_nu - beta_nu*gamma_nu). This is > 0 unless w is constant.

Specialisation:
- Take w = Σ m_mu u_mu with real m and the normalised first-kind integrals. Their period across a_nu is pi*i*δ_{mu,nu} and across b_nu is a_{mu,nu}.
- Then A^(nu) = m_nu*pi*i, so alpha_nu = 0 and gamma_nu = pi*m_nu.
- Also B_nu = Σ_mu a_{mu,nu} m_mu, so beta_nu = Re Σ_mu a_{mu,nu} m_mu.
- Hence the Dirichlet integral = -pi Σ_nu m_nu*beta_nu = Re(-pi Σ_{mu,nu} a_{mu,nu} m_mu m_nu) > 0.
- That is, Re Σ a_{mu,nu} m_mu m_nu < 0 for all real m ≠ 0: the real part of the period form is negative definite. This guarantees convergence of Riemann's theta series Σ exp(Σ a m m + 2 Σ m u).

Marginal footnote (+): the integral ∫∫(mu_x nu_y - mu_y nu_x) dS is the area, counted with multiplicity, of the region of the w-plane covered by the values of w on S'. In other words, the Jacobian-area interpretation.

Fragmentary remark: the functions u and their periods are thereby determined by S' up to additive constants.

(B) Number of zeros of theta.
- theta(u - e), viewed as a function on S', is single-valued and everywhere finite.
- The zeros of theta can be found from ∫ d log theta. Taken around S', this integral is unchanged if one removes regions where theta ≠ 0.
- So it equals the sum of the integrals around the zeros, i.e. 2*pi*i × (number of simple zeros).
- On the other hand, it equals Σ ∫(d log theta^+ - d log theta^-) over all cuts a, b, c.
- On the cuts where log theta jumps only by a constant, the contribution is 0.
- On the cuts where theta acquires the factor exp(-2(u_nu - e_nu) - a_{nu,nu}), the difference is 2 du_nu (up to orientation). Its integral along the line is the complementary period pi*i, giving 2*pi*i per cut.
- Total = p*2*pi*i, so theta has exactly p zeros (eta_1..eta_p, as on the preceding page), provided it does not vanish identically.

The last line ('Und die Lage der ... Linien a und b') breaks off.
errors: In (B) the page says the integrals along lines b and c vanish and those along a_nu give 2∫du_nu = 2*pi*i. This is consistent with the preceding page only with a and b interchanged. There log theta jumps by a constant across a_nu, and by 2(u_nu - e_nu)/... + a_{nu,nu} across b_nu. Also, part (A) on this page uses the fact that integrating along a_nu yields the b-period. So it should be the a- and c-cuts that contribute 0, and b_nu that gives 2∫_{b_nu} du_nu = 2*pi*i (the a-period of u_nu). Most likely a slip of the letters in the draft; alternatively it is a transcription issue.
Orientation signs in (B) are not tracked: 2∫du_nu vs -2∫du_nu depends on the side convention. Only the absolute count p matters, and the published version handles this correctly.
The vanishing of the c-cut contributions in (A) is not stated explicitly. It holds because ∫dnu around a closed c-cut is 0, given the canonical dissection.

Strict positivity requires w nonconstant, i.e. m ≠ 0; this is implicit. Also, the zero count implicitly assumes theta(u - e) is not identically zero on the surface. Riemann addresses this in the published paper.

results.what: Dirichlet integral of Re w equals Σ(alpha_nu delta_nu - beta_nu gamma_nu) > 0, computed via Green's theorem and the jumps across canonical cuts
results.modern_name: Riemann bilinear inequality (positivity part of the Riemann bilinear relations)

results.what: Re Σ a_{mu,nu} m_mu m_nu < 0 for real m ≠ 0, i.e. the period matrix has negative definite real part (Siegel upper half-space condition in Riemann's normalisation)
results.modern_name: Positive-definiteness of Im(tau) for the normalised period matrix (Riemann's second bilinear relation), ensuring theta convergence

results.what: Interpretation of ∫∫ (mu_x nu_y - mu_y nu_x) dS as the area covered by the image of w
results.modern_name: Jacobian / area formula for holomorphic maps
results.usually_credited_to: classical; this remark appears in Riemann's 1857 paper

results.what: theta(u - e) has exactly p zeros on T', counted by the argument principle along the canonical dissection
results.modern_name: Riemann's theorem on the zeros of the theta function (theta divisor has degree g)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material published almost verbatim in Riemann's 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (§§20-22). The negative definiteness of Re(a) via the Dirichlet integral, the area remark, and the count of p zeros of theta are all well known as his. The only items of note are drafting details and an apparent a/b slip.

transcription_corrections: Line 'Die Integrale durch die Linien b und c sind =0, die Integrale durch a_nu gleich 2∫du_nu = 2πi': the image does seem to read this way, but mathematically (and per the previous page) a and b should be interchanged. Flag as a probable slip in the manuscript rather than a transcription error.

'Die Function ϑ bleibt allenthalben endlich' – the image supports 'Die Function ϑ bleibt allenthalben endlich'. The following 'Für einen Punkt von S', wo ϑ ... unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung wird' likely reads 'Die Anzahl der Punkte von S', wo ϑ unendlich klein von der ersten Ordnung wird, kann durch Betrachtung des Integrals ∫d log ϑ gefunden werden'.

In the marginal note (+), 'den Inhalt des Flächentheils' is better read as 'den Inhalt des Flächentheils ... aus, welchen die Gesammtheit der Werthe, welche w innerhalb S' annimmt, auf der w-Ebene repräsentirt' (the area-of-image remark).
'B_nu' in the line 'A^(nu) = m_nu pi i, B_nu = ...' is written B with subscript nu in the manuscript, inconsistent with B^(nu) above; this is notational only.
'Integration ... gleich dem ∫mu dnu' – the struck/marginal word under the line is plausibly 'durch partielle Integration' / 'nach dem Green'schen Satze'; uncertain.
